basis.basis: OSR diagnostic moving-load and handling geometry scenarios only. Existing three-car axle reference is not accepted six-car railway loading. No new material resistance, code loading, lifting insert or rig configuration is adopted.

diagnostic_load_case.loading: AW2 planning reference, equal mass and passengers per car

limitations: The diagnostic uses the retained three-car planning reference, not an accepted six-car Baghdad loading. Multiplier is an OSR sensitivity, not a code dynamic factor

Gross prismatic uncracked section, full-force straight tendons and retained local loss hypothesis. Transmission/end zones, compression limits, reinforcement, shear/torsion/fatigue, nonlinear response and railway dynamic interaction remain open

Moving moment/reaction events and continuous sagging peak cover one-dimensional downward axle loads. Fibre stress extrema are sampled at the declared stations; no continuous stress or deflection envelope is claimed

Handling overhang bending and symmetric leg-force hypotheses omit tilt, unequal sharing, local inserts, breakout, transverse torsion, transport, suction and wind. Additional reinforcement/attachments and complete rig mass remain unknown

One long spreader plus two transverse distributors is an enquiry concept. Capacity depends on span, sling angles, component configuration and supplier approval; headline model capacity cannot select the rig

continuous_peak.method: entry/exit/under-axle branches with quadratic stationary points

basis.basis: OSR finite planning campaign, not measured production or supplier cycle data. Consecutive operating days with a 16 h window assuming two 8 h team shifts; handover/breaks are unmodelled. Curing and storage dwell use elapsed clock hours. Casting dedicates mixer/crane/crew for the entire continuous pour block, without overlapping mixing and pouring.
basis.mixer_model_enquiry: Rapid RP1000 planetary; useful batch output and mix cycle unconfirmed
unknown: supplier-accepted batch output and continuous pour window
mix design, strength/maturity release and measured process durations
reinforcement inventory and first-article acceptance
haulage payload, permitted route and delivery windows
full workforce/shift/calendar and maintenance strategy
plant commissioning and all Baghdad installed costs

limitations: Finite first-come list schedule; neither steady-state capacity nor an optimum
Batch output, durations, release maturity and shift pattern are unmeasured planning assumptions
Casting dedicates crane and mixer for one continuous block; no mix/pour overlap or hot-concrete queue
No adopted lift plan, transport route, workforce agreement, reliability distribution or accepted output evidence

basis.basis: Nominal first-station post/baseplate and soil-interface research cases. Geometry, stiffness and loads are preliminary; no material, anchor, ground or physical release is implied.

limitations: Rigid baseplate and nominal gross-bar springs omit plate flexibility, thread roots, bond/embedment, preload, prying and concrete failure
Gross rectangular grout contact ignores anchor-hole exclusion; nominal weld-line demands omit access, corner/gap effects, stiffness and resistance
Post load is final initial-force rail imperfection response; strongback stressing/release torsion, rail selfweight and operating loads need separate combined stages
Two independent bow signs are combined at each matching station; maxima from different stations are not combined
Pad pressure is a static uniaxial equilibrium demand, not soil resistance, sliding, settlement, reinforcement or anchor design
Actual site, grout, connection and anchor stiffness/resistance are unmeasured; hypothetical interface sensitivity cannot qualify ground springs
Gross first-order elastic spatial frame; rigid joints/offsets and finite linear six-axis base springs are unmeasured hypotheses
Shear deformation, distortion, warping, local holes/diaphragm stresses, joint slip, contact and material/geometric nonlinearity remain open
Retained second-order independent rail failures are separate mandatory checks; this model cannot clear them
Base spring wrenches include coupled forces and moments; the earlier one-axis anchor/pad screens cannot qualify these biaxial/torsional demands
Native complete bed contains steel geometry and supplier/foundation envelopes; rail splices, mould, product, reinforcement, crane and site qualification remain open

basis.allocation: Linear transverse lever weights preserve total axial force, transverse first moment and vertical couple. Mirrored strand forces at opposite bed ends give opposite generalized rotation loads.
basis.scope: Static research force states only; no adopted stressing/unloading procedure, concrete transfer, release maturity or physical qualification.

limitations: Linear transverse lever allocation of rail axial forces/couples is a hypothesis; strongback torsion/warping and 3-D connection stiffness remain unresolved
Opposite end rotation loads assume mirrored tendon fields at the two bed ends; independent end operation is unmodelled
Quasistatic strand unloading is a bed-force hypothesis, not an approved release procedure or strand-to-concrete transmission solution
Ideal end pins remain externally grounded. Their vertical demand is reported; axial closure, foundation resistance and actual end details are unqualified
Rail gravity is included; strongback/mould/service weights, thermal actions, preload, losses, jacking overpull and dynamics remain unmodelled
One-axis post/grout/anchor/pad screens retain fixed ideal spring properties; no self-consistent nonlinear ground or local resistance acceptance
Only the specified stressing endpoints and unloading increments are evaluated; no continuous transient envelope is claimed
